name: sparda
description: The trust layer for AI-written code. AI writes, SPARDA proves. Deterministic, offline behavior proofs + a live gate for AI edits, right in the editor.

commands.title: Apocalypse — findings to the Problems panel
Install the gate into Claude Code
Enforce — plan a verified boundary check (dry run)

walkthroughs.title: Prove your backend with SPARDA
walkthroughs.description: Three steps: install the engine, get a verdict, then freeze it as the baseline every AI edit is proven against.

steps.title: Install the engine
steps.description:
This extension ships no engine — it is a thin bridge over the `sparda-mcp` CLI, so its verdict can never drift from the CLI's. Install it into your workspace and the extension picks it up.
[Install sparda-mcp](command:sparda.install)

steps.title: Get a verdict
steps.description:
SPARDA compiles your routes into a behavior graph and reports what it can and cannot prove. The status bar carries the verdict; an analysis that did not run reads UNKNOWN, never green.
[Prove workspace](command:sparda.prove)

steps.title: Arm the gate
steps.description:
Freeze the current behavior as the accepted baseline. From then on, every edit — yours or an agent's — is proven against it, and a removed guard is caught in the loop rather than in review.
[Arm the baseline](command:sparda.gate.arm)

sparda.command.markdownDescription: How to invoke the SPARDA CLI. Leave empty to use the workspace's own `node_modules/.bin/sparda`, falling back to `npx --no-install sparda-mcp`. A bare global on `PATH` is deliberately never picked up: the version that proves the code should be the version the project pinned.
